To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found evidence of an excess of double-coincidence events at about 511 keV, which we interpret as a possible indication of the Internal Pair Production in 241Am.
we have observed an excess of double-coincidence events in faced pairs of NaI detectors, and that this excess is consistent with an IPP process in the alpha decay of $^{241}$Am.

we have observed an excess of events with respect to background in a new search for correlated $e^{ +}e^{-}$ pair production in the $ \beta$ decay of 41Ca, and that we have obtained a relative activity $\ lambda$ for the Internal Pair production in the $a$ decay of 24Am of the same order as the previous determinations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the $\alpha$-particle decay of 241 Am, which is one of the most important sources of natural radiation.

the search for new phenomena in the $\alpha $ decay of 241 Am, which is the most suitable source of low energy photons and electrons for the detection of hypothetical new particles and/or interactions.

the study of the $e^{+}$ and $e^{-}$ emission in the $\alpha-$decay of 241Am, which can be interpreted as the decay of a neutral particle, the so-called Majoron, which is a hypothetical neutral particle, emitted in the decay of a neutrino, and which can couple to the electron and electron neutrino.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, while the present result cannot be considered conclusive for the existence of a new effect, it represents the best measurement of the IPP process in the $\alpha $ decay of 241 Am, obtained by a new technique.
, although a small excess of events with respect to the expected background is observed, the experimental result cannot be considered a positive signal of IPP.
the present result is consistent with the previous determinations and with the theoretical predictions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the present result is consistent with the hypothesis of the IPP process in the $\alpha$
decay of 241Am, but no firm conclusion can be drawn.
the experimental data show a clear excess of correlated e+e-pairs, which can be interpreted as an evidence for IPP in the alpha decay of $^{241}$Am.

the present experimental result, together with the previous ones obtained by the DAMA and the EDELWEISS Collaborations, do not support the existence of a signal of IPP, but they are consistent with a background level of IPP in the $\alpha-$decay of 241Am of the order of $10^{-9}$.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we are now in the position to perform an underground experiment to search for correlated e$^+$e$^-$pairs from the decay of $^{241}$Am with a sensitivity to a few events/yr, which is about two orders of magnitude better than the present limit.
we have shown that the IPP can be measured in the $ \beta$-decay of 241Am with a high degree of accuracy, and that this can be used to test the Standard Model of electroweak interactions.
we have shown that the IPP rate in 241Am can be measured with a precision of the order of 10% by using the DAMA/Libra set-up.
